## Added

`inspect` has two new `llm_reasons` values. A caller that routes on
`llm_recommended` needs no change; one that branches on the slugs should learn
both.

- `vector_drawing`: the page's content is line work its text layer carries at
  most the labels of — a map, diagram, chart or plan (10 or more paths that
  curve or run diagonally, or 1000 or more paths of any kind), or text drawn
  as outlines (almost no text, no images, 50 or more paths). A table's rules
  are straight and stay unflagged.
- `page_unloadable`: pdfium could not load the page (a damaged page object or
  page tree).

## Fixed

- `inspect` no longer fails a whole document because one page will not load.
  A PDF whose page tree lists its own Catalog as a page stopped at that page
  with `PdfiumLibraryInternalError`; the page is now listed with
  `page_unloadable`, its error under a new `errors` object (absent when every
  page loaded) and on stderr, and every other page is inspected as usual.
- `image_coverage` counts images inside Form XObjects. Their bounds are in the
  form's space, so they were left out, and a scan that the scanner wraps in a
  form — with its OCR text — read as 0% image: not a scan, not `image_heavy`.
  Such an image now counts as its share of the form's drawn extent times the
  form's area on the page.
- `inspect` sees what annotations draw. A page whose content lives only in
  annotation appearances — a chart pasted as a markup box, its title as a
  text box, over an empty page — read as blank and was never flagged. Images
  inside annotations now count toward `image_count` and `image_coverage`
  (against the annotation's rectangle) and their paths toward
  `vector_drawing`, so such a page is `no_text_layer` + `image_heavy`.
- `image_heavy` starts at 10% image coverage instead of 20%. A map, photo or
  diagram filling a tenth of the page carries content the text layer cannot
  see; on a routing benchmark those pages needed a vision pass about as
  often as the ones above 20%.
- `structured --ocr scans` reads a page whose whole-page picture is drawn
  first with visible text laid over it — a scanner's OCR overlay — by OCR as
  well, and keeps whichever reading has more real words. A typewritten table
  of contents whose overlay read "15-S-" and "t e evaluat" now reads its page
  numbers and titles; a digital page on a full-page background keeps its text
  layer.

On a routing benchmark (398 documents, 18,700 pages with a saved
vision reading), pages flagged `llm_recommended` rise from 46% to 54%, and the
share of pages that needed a vision pass which the flag catches rises from 76%
to 88%. Routed on these labels alone, a consumer matches its former router — its
own page heuristics plus 0.18.4's flags — on pages judged from their images
(81% of needed pages caught, averaged over five samples) with 4% fewer vision
calls. The text bench and scorecard are unchanged; the fourteen reviewed
dossiers differ only in each page's `routing_signals`.
